basics.name: Priscila de Azevedo Drummond
basics.label: PhD Candidate in Industrial Engineering & Operations Research
basics.summary: PhD candidate in Industrial Engineering at Northeastern University, specializing in network optimization and operations research for social good, with a focus on anti-human trafficking and labor rights. Teaching Fellow, 2026 COE Outstanding Graduate Teaching Award recipient, and passionate advocate for inclusive, active-learning pedagogy in engineering education.

education.institution: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul

work.name: Northeastern University
work.position: Teaching Fellow – OR 6205: Deterministic Operations Research
work.summary: Sole instructor of record for graduate-level Deterministic Operations Research. Designed curriculum, assessments, and active learning materials from scratch using backward design principles.
highlights: Designed full course with project-based learning, collaborative board work, and multi-format feedback
Recipient of 2026 COE Outstanding Graduate Teaching Award
Implemented self-assessment rubrics and rework opportunities to build student learning autonomy

work.name: Northeastern University – Operations Research & Social Justice Lab
work.summary: Develop network interdiction models to combat labor trafficking in U.S. agricultural supply chains. Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams of researchers, policymakers, and practitioners.
highlights: Published in PLOS ONE (2024) on multilevel regression modeling of H-2A labor violations
Presented at INFORMS Annual Meetings 2022–2025
Network interdiction model for multi-agency antitrafficking collaboration (working paper)

work.name: Northeastern University
work.summary: TA for Quality Assurance (IE 4516) and Lean Concepts and Applications (IE 5617) under Prof. Hugh McManus and Prof. Andrei Guschin.
highlights: Developed new instructional materials and slides; taught 1–2 recitation sections per term
Supported 45–46 students per section; maintained office hours and provided detailed feedback
Student feedback: 'Your communication is articulate and you have a natural warmth that makes us feel comfortable.'

work.name: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
work.summary: TA for Operations Research, Manufacturing Production and Control, and Engineering Management under Prof. Hiram Moya.
highlights: Created and delivered tutorial sessions and instructional videos during COVID-19 pandemic transition
Implemented personalized feedback systems and held regular office hours
Taught 18–21 students per section across three undergraduate courses

work.name: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
work.summary: Engineered Bayesian optimization model integrating cost-benefit analysis with statistical predictors to improve identification of human trafficking at U.S. border checkpoints.
highlights: Developed decision support tool for U.S. ports of entry with anti-human trafficking focus
Published in DSI Proceedings (2020)
Presented at Texas A&M Coastal Bend Mathematics and Statistics Conference (2021)

work.name: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul
work.summary: Partnered with Rio Grande do Sul's Secretary of Security to optimize resource allocation in crime prevention and survivor support networks.
highlights: Conducted large-scale data analysis of crime and social service metrics across 450+ cities
Implemented DEA models informing policy decisions affecting 10+ million residents
Delivered bi-weekly research seminars for industry-partnered student work

work.name: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro
work.summary: Engineering, Design, and Technology Curriculum Coordinator for a project-based learning model school. Developed and taught experiential learning curriculum integrating engineering principles with creative design for students ages 11–16.
highlights: Managed interdisciplinary team of 10–15 undergraduate interns
Taught boat design and construction to 90+ students per year
Organized 4 events per year serving 2,000+ community members

work.name: COMLURB – Sanitation Company
work.summary: Strategic budgeting and financial analysis for municipal sanitation company in Rio de Janeiro.
highlights: Secured 100% budget approval at annual Town Hall meetings
Reduced contracts and inventory costs by 30% through auditing and new inventory policies
Developed analytical frameworks informing C-suite strategic planning

projects.name: Collaboration in Antitrafficking Efforts: A Network Interdiction Problem
projects.summary: Models how collaboration between law enforcement agencies improves labor trafficking interdiction outcomes using network optimization. Working paper with K.L. Maass.
highlights: Presented at INFORMS Annual Meeting 2025
Demonstrates that multi-agency cooperation substantially improves detection rates

projects.name: OR 6205: Deterministic Operations Research – Course Design
projects.summary: Designed and taught a full graduate-level OR course as Teaching Fellow using backward design, active learning, and project-based assessments. Developed all course materials including syllabus, in-class exercises, case studies, and grading rubrics.
highlights: 2026 COE Outstanding Graduate Teaching Award
Student-led real-world LP case analysis as central course project
Iterative feedback model with rework opportunities built into grading
